title: Day 782: Thousands March in Culiacán for Peace on Second Anniversary of Chapitos–Mayos War
detail: Thousands of Culiacán residents marched on Sunday, September 13, 2026, to demand security and peace, two years after the Chapitos–Mayos war began on September 9, 2024. The mobilization started with a 7:00 AM mass followed by a march from La Lomita, and included search collectives for missing persons and families of victims carrying signs reading 'We don't want fear, we want peace' and 'When a mother cries, we all cry.' Organizers said the conflict has left more than 3,000 people killed and thousands more disappeared or displaced. The march came a day after ten homicides were recorded across Sinaloa state — four in Culiacán, five in Mazatlán and one in Escuinapa — underscoring that violence had not abated ahead of the demonstration.
